bihar_raw_news.title: Museum Ranking 2026: Bihar museum secures top position in Asia, ranks 9th globally
bihar_raw_news.content: Museum Ranking 2026: Bihar museum secures top position in Asia, ranks 9th globally The ranking identifies 10 museums in Asia, with institutions from Japan, Malaysia, South Korea, Indonesia and India featuring on the list Join Our WhatsApp Channel Business Today Desk Updated Oct 28, 2026 3:00 AM IST Bihar Museum is the only Indian institution featured among the 100 museums selected worldwide The Bihar Museum in Patna has earned international recognition after securing the ninth position in the World’s 100 Best Museums 2026 list published by travel platform Worth a Journey. The museum has also been ranked the best in Asia, placing Bihar’s rich historical and cultural heritage in the global spotlight. Advertisement According to the ranking, Bihar Museum is the only Indian institution featured among the 100 museums selected worldwide. Its ninth-place finish puts it among some of the world’s most prominent cultural institutions, highlighting its role in preserving and showcasing India’s heritage. Read More READ THIS: No phone, no cars, almost no people. Here is why tourists are paying ₹1.06 lakh to visit this ‘Ghost Island Bihar museum among global leaders The 2026 list features museums dedicated to art, history, science, technology and open-air collections across different continents. Mexico City’s Museo Nacional de Antropología secured the first position, followed by Spain’s Museo del Prado in second place and Denmark’s Louisiana Museum of Modern Art in third. The State Hermitage Museum in Russia and Vienna’s Kunsthistorisches Museum also featured among the top 10 institutions. Bihar Museum’s inclusion in this group marks a significant achievement for India’s museum and cultural tourism sector. Advertisement The ranking identifies 10 museums in Asia, with institutions from Japan, Malaysia, South Korea, Indonesia and India featuring on the list. Bihar Museum emerged as the continent’s highest-ranked institution, ahead of other prominent Asian museums. Showcasing Bihar’s rich cultural heritage Established in Patna, Bihar Museum is a modern state museum that traces the region’s history from the Stone Age to contemporary times. Its collection includes ancient sculptures, coins, manuscripts, archaeological artefacts and regional folk art. The museum’s galleries are arranged chronologically, helping visitors understand Bihar’s historical development and cultural evolution. Its spacious premises, open courtyards and landscaped lawns complement the exhibitions. ALSO READ: Neil Armstrong inspired him as a boy. 57 years later, he spent $400,000 to save the astronaut’s childhood home Advertisement Among its key attractions are the ancient sculpture galleries, a dedicated children’s gallery and a regional folk art section. The museum also features a short film on history, making it an educational destination for students, researchers and tourists. Boost for Bihar’s tourism potential The international recognition could strengthen Patna’s position as a cultural tourism destination and encourage more domestic and international visitors to explore Bihar’s heritage. The ranking also highlights the growing importance of modern museums in presenting historical collections through engaging visitor experiences. The Bihar government has introduced a 100-point performance assessment index to evaluate banks operating in the state. IDFC FIRST Bank topped the ranking with 74 points. Key Points Performance Assessment Index: Banks have been classified into three zones based on their scores: Green Zone: Includes 11 banks scoring 50 or above. Yellow Zone: Comprises 7 banks. Red Zone: Contains several banks, including public sector banks. Annual Credit Plan 2026–27: Bihar has set a credit disbursement target of ₹4.95 lakh crore . By 30 th September 2026, banks had disbursed ₹1.89 lakh crore, achieving 38.25% of the target. Credit disbursement to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) reached ₹84,091 crore, while agricultural credit disbursement stood at ₹43,967 crore. Credit-Deposit Ratio (CDR): Bihar's CDR stood at 60.17% as of 30 th September 2026 . The state government urged banks to increase lending within the state, clear pending loan applications and improve credit access, particularly under the Kisan Credit Card and PM Vishwakarma schemes. Credit-Deposit Ratio The Credit-Deposit Ratio (CDR) is the ratio of a bank's total loans and advances to its total deposits, expressed as a percentage. It indicates the extent to which deposits mobilised by banks are converted into credit. Naz Ozair, an engineer from Muzaffarpur, Bihar, developed a patented technology to manufacture eco-friendly utensils from corn husks, promoting plastic alternatives and rural entrepreneurship. Key Points Innovation: Naz Ozair, a resident of Muradpur village, Kurhani block, Muzaffarpur, developed a technique to convert discarded corn husks into cups, plates, bowls, glasses, straws and bags. Startup: He established MNO Swadeshi India Pvt. Ltd. , which was incorporated on 5 th September, 2023, to manufacture these products. Environmental Significance: The innovation promotes agricultural-waste utilisation and offers alternatives to single-use plastics. Government Support: The Bihar government encourages rural innovations under the Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) and Lohia Swachh Bihar Abhiyan . Single-Use Plastic SUPs are disposable plastic items designed to be used once or for a short period before being discarded or recycled. Examples: Packaging materials, bottles, polythene bags, coffee cups, cling film, trash bags and food packaging. From 1 st July 2022 , India prohibited 21 identified single-use plastic (SUP) items with low utility and high littering potential under the Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules, 2021. Manufacturers, importers and brand owners are required to ensure the collection and recycling of post-consumer plastic waste. Implementation Challenges: Limited alternatives, high costs for MSMEs and the continued use of thin plastic carry bags hinder effective enforcement.
